finding.claim: The /transfer endpoint does not validate that amount is positive. An authenticated user can send a negative amount and drain the recipient's balance into their own. The sibling /withdraw handler has the check (`amount <= 0`) at line 21; /transfer lacks it.
finding.source: request.json["amount"] (bank.py:10) and request.json["to"] (bank.py:9), controlled by the authenticated caller

trace.note: amount read from JSON with no type or sign validation
the only check is BAL[g.user] < amount; with a negative amount this is always false, so the check passes
BAL[g.user] -= negative increases the caller's balance
BAL[to] += negative decreases the victim's balance, which can go negative. The victim's consent is not required.

finding.guards_checked: Balance check at line 11 is bypassed by a negative amount. There is no sign check, unlike /withdraw at line 21. There is no recipient consent or authorization check. I found no other controls in the file.

verdict.guard_found: Only the balance check `BAL[g.user] < amount` at bank.py:11, which a negative amount always passes. There is no sign or type check, and no recipient consent check. The `amount <= 0` check exists only in /withdraw (bank.py:21). g.user is not set in this file, so authentication happens elsewhere or not at all.
verdict.reason: bank.py:11 only checks `BAL[g.user] < amount`, so a negative amount passes. Lines 13-14 then raise the caller's balance and lower the recipient's, and /transfer has no equivalent of the `amount <= 0` guard at bank.py:21. Any user who can call /transfer can exploit it, and no authorization control blocks it.
